population: female college students 17–29 with regular or irregular cycles; all mild acne (grade I–II)
phases_compared: menstrual vs intermenstrual (x regular vs irregular cycles)
measure: 16S rRNA sequencing, right-cheek swab; alpha (Shannon, PD) and beta diversity (unweighted UniFrac)
main_result: Beta diversity: only Irregular-Menstrual vs Regular-Menstrual differed (R² = 0.0179, p < 0.001); no significant difference between the two regular subgroups (menstrual vs interval) or the two irregular subgroups; alpha diversity Irregular-Menstrual higher than Regular-Interval (p < 0.01)
risk_of_bias: some concerns: no hormone confirmation; contraception not addressed; phases limited to menstrual vs interval
notes: Phase effect only within irregular-cycle group; regular cyclers showed no phase difference. Small effect sizes (R² ≈ 0.02).

population: healthy Chinese women 24–29, regular 26–30 day cycles, no acne
phases_compared: ovulation vs early luteal (all); follicular, ovulation, early luteal, late luteal (high-sebum group)
measure: Sebutape sebum lipid composition (GC-MS, LC-MS), forehead and cheeks
main_result: Main effects due to skin type; menstrual-phase effect on high-sebum forehead lipids significant by ASCA (p = 0.003); sebum-type lipids (branched FFAs, C15–18 SFAs, MUFAs) peaked at ovulation and declined at early luteal; TGs and long-chain SFAs higher at early luteal
risk_of_bias: some concerns: phase by urinary LH tests but n=19 per group; contraception exclusion not explicit; industry funded (P&G)
notes: Composition, not sebum output. Includes SZ95 sebocyte in-vitro arm (not extracted).

population: female graduate students, regular 21–35 day cycles

risk_of_bias: high: self-report recall; no comparison phase; contraceptive users (4.6%) not excluded

population: healthy women 18–65; reproductive group mean age 27.06, regular 25–31 day cycles

population: healthy women, mean age 23.36, no hormonal contraception ≥3 months

risk_of_bias: low: LH-confirmed, pill users excluded, blind to hypothesis; small n (22)
notes: Changes statistically significant but below human visual detection threshold.
